page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.large is a general-purpose virtual instance configured under the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by custom AWS silicon built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, ensuring consistent compute execution without hyper-threading contention. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a 36 MB L3 cache pool.

Hardware resource boundaries are tailored for lightweight networked operations. The instance does not include local NVMe or ephemeral storage, requiring reliance on external Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for operating system disks and persistent file layers. No GPU accelerators are attached. Networking capacity provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, supporting typical distributed communication for small workloads without dedicated interface overprovisioning.

Benchmark data reflects solid single-threaded architectural efficiency alongside the strict throughput limits of a dual-core topology. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression scores in the top tier, while single-core Geekbench and stress-ng ratings register in the average middle percentile. PassMark database operations also maintain average rankings. However, multi-core scaling is inherently constrained by the low core count, resulting in lower scores in multi-core compiling, ray tracing, and aggregate stress testing. Memory bandwidth remains adequate for standard workloads, showing 56.38 GB/sec in uncached large-block reads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8gb.large instance offers an economical entry point into ARMv9 computing without overcommitting on memory or storage tiers. The absence of local drives and hardware accelerators reduces unnecessary overhead for horizontal architectures. It serves as an appropriate deployment target for containerized microservices, light backend APIs, modest Redis caching tiers, CI/CD runners, and general low-traffic enterprise utilities.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.large is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton eighth-generation processor technology. It features 2 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of memory to provide a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, with no integrated local storage and no hardware GPUs. Network throughput is provisioned with a 4 Gbps baseline. Benchmark evaluations indicate respectable single-core performance, highlighted by strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression and average Geekbench single-core execution, though aggregate multi-core and vector compute show weak scaling due to the two-core limit. As an entry-level general-purpose profile, it provides cost-efficient baseline throughput for microservices, lightweight web serving, and small database workloads.
